item.title: US stocks rise as investors snap up beaten-down AI stocks
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes experienced gains after the Thanksgiving holiday as investors returned to the market. There was notable volatility in AI-related stocks, influenced by Nvidia's CEO and Anthropic's IPO price situation. Despite the positive movement, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are still on track for their worst November since 2008. Trading volumes remained thin due to the holiday and outnumbering advancing issues reported positive market sentiment.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Wall Street’s main indexes rose on Friday, putting them on course for weekly gains as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and bought beaten-down artificial intelligence-linked stocks, Reuters reported.The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 361.11 points, or 0.72%, at 50,544.06. The S&P 500 gained 51.78 points, or 0.74%, to 7,235.66, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 204.05 points, or 0.87%, to 23,789.86. All but one S&P 500 sector traded higher, with information technology stocks providing the biggest boost.US shares have swung sharply this week. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s return and Anthropic’s brief fall below its IPO price added to volatility in AI-related stocks. Investors have weighed opportunities to buy after a steep sell-off against concerns about soaring costs, heavy borrowing and whether large AI investments will generate sufficient returns.“Investors felt that the sell-off we saw going into last Friday was overdone. It would be more of a steady push up from here, possibly,” David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, told Reuters.Despite this week’s turbulence, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for their best weeks since April and August, respectively. The Dow was headed for its strongest week since April 2025.Chipmakers that had been hit hard this month recovered some ground. Micron and Marvell each gained more than 2%, while the broader chip gauge rose 1.3%. AI-linked companies including data-storage firm Sandisk, optical-products maker Lumentum and server maker Dell also advanced.Large technology companies rose as well. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta Platforms and Oracle gained between 1% and 2.7%. Nvidia, however, fell 1.3%, leaving the stock nearly 40% below its October record high.The gains have done little to reverse November’s losses. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq remained on track for their worst November since 2008, amid concerns about tougher AI regulation following the Democrats’ midterm election victory and expectations that monetary policy will remain restrictive.Traders were also pricing in a December Federal Reserve interest rate hike after data this week showed the US economy grew faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated further in October.Among other stocks, gold and silver miners rallied as precious-metal prices recovered from recent losses. Newmont gained 3.6%, while the Global X Silver Miners ETF advanced 4%.Altria fell 1.8% after the US Marlboro maker said it was considering an all-cash bid for Imperial Brands. It also said it was discussing a deal involving part of the British tobacco group’s business with another party.Vertex Pharmaceuticals slid nearly 10% after the US Food and Drug Administration extended its review of the company’s kidney-disease drug by up to three months.Trading volumes were thin following Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday, with US equity markets open for a half-day session on Friday. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by 3.47 to 1 on the New York Stock Exchange and 3.15 to 1 on the Nasdaq.The S&P 500 recorded five new 52-week highs and no new lows. The Nasdaq Composite posted 22 new highs and 31 new lows.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Crude oil prices near $97 as West Asia tensions revive supply fears; OPEC+ meeting in focus
item.description: Crude oil rose to a near three-week high as attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping in West Asia revived concerns about supply disruptions. Brent traded near $97 a barrel ahead of Sunday’s OPEC+ meeting, where producers are expected to review their 2027 output strategy. Expectations of ample global supply continue to limit the rally.
item.dc:creator: Akash Podishetti
item.content:encoded: Crude oil prices climbed to their highest level in nearly three weeks on Friday, putting Brent crude on track to snap a three-week losing streak, as escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia raised concerns over disruptions to global oil supplies. The rebound comes ahead of a crucial OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29, where producers are expected to discuss their 2027 output strategy.Brent crude futures rose 0.8% to $97.30 a barrel on Friday, their highest level since November 9, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained 2.6% to $85.85 a barrel compared with Wednesday’s close, according to Reuters. There was no settlement for WTI on Thursday because of the US Thanksgiving holiday.The rally follows a sharp recovery in prices over the past few sessions, driven by fresh attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial shipping in the Middle East. Brent had fallen below $88 a barrel earlier in the week as concerns over an emerging global supply surplus outweighed geopolitical risks.The latest escalation has brought the possibility of supply disruptions back into focus. Yemen’s Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery, one of the kingdom’s largest refining facilities and a major crude export hub. The group also claimed attacks on other Saudi targets.Separately, Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery temporarily suspended some operations after a projectile struck the facility on Thursday, killing a worker and injuring several others, according to the kingdom’s Energy Ministry.Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz has also come under pressure. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said two tankers had exploded and caught fire after striking sea mines near Oman’s Khasab port while attempting to cross the strait. The waterway is a critical transit route for global energy supplies, carrying a substantial share of the world’s seaborne oil trade.The attacks have raised concerns that the recovery in crude exports from the Persian Gulf could be disrupted, adding a geopolitical risk premium to oil prices. Analysts at ANZ said Brent could move above $100 a barrel, although such a move would increasingly require evidence of an actual constraint on deliverable supplies.Also Read | MCX silver prices hit 6% upper circuit at Rs 1.54 lakh/kg. Why are people buying the white metal on Black Friday?However, expectations of ample global supplies continue to limit the upside in crude prices. Brent remains significantly below its levels earlier in the month, despite the recent rebound. The International Energy Agency has flagged the possibility of a supply surplus in the fourth quarter, while expectations of rising production have weighed on market sentiment.US crude inventories rose by 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million barrels in the week ended November 20, according to the Energy Information Administration. The increase was smaller than analysts’ expectations of a 1.5-million-barrel build, offering some support to prices.OPEC+ meeting in focusInvestors will now turn their attention to Sunday’s OPEC+ meeting, where member countries are expected to review production policy for 2027. The group is likely to maintain its existing output targets through at least the first quarter of next year, according to sources cited by Reuters.The meeting comes amid competing pressures for the producer alliance. While geopolitical disruptions have increased near-term supply risks, concerns about a potential global surplus could make producers cautious about raising output.Oil prices will depend on whether the latest geopolitical developments translate into sustained supply disruptions or remain largely a risk premium in futures markets.
